Seen • Just now
Good question. You actually don’t need much to get great results.
The soil already includes slow-release fertilizer, so nothing is needed for the first year.
After that, you can add a liquid houseplant fertilizer during the growing months, diluted to about 1/4 strength and poured into the reservoir.
If the soil settles over time, you can lightly top it up with coco coir or a light indoor potting mix.
Optional: a small humidifier or pebble tray nearby can help create a more humid microenvironment. 
So the plant itself is the main investment. The extras are simple and optional.
